title: The Club Morocco and later New York troubles
summary: The band settled at the Club Morocco for about three months; Schremp mentions its later sparse New York audiences.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Is it a logical step to go into the Ben Pollack days at this stage? The recording session that he switched on you.
Those days followed the San Francisco days, with the onset of the new writing, the move to Hollywood and to the Club Morocco; that's where the band settled in and became what it was.
How long were you at the Morocco?
Oh gosh, it must have been about three months. It was a long stay.
It was in New York. Were the crowds so sparse that the band had to applaud their own tunes on the air shots?
I have no idea what happened in New York.
I think that was at the Vanity Fair, 1948 or something, one of the later bands. Business was so bad that when the tune was over, the band would all applaud for the radio audience.
I never heard that. I can understand it. When they came back from California?
I don't know what happened to them. When I left I left; that was it.

That was on this monster twenty-three piece band with the bassoons and things. The audience was not quite sure how to deal with that, having never heard jazz harp, which of course there wasn't anyway.
Anyway, when you went into Club Morocco, that's a pause for you.
When we went into the Club Morocco--now using my own pause--what happened when we went into the Club Morocco?
At that point the band was a hero or you were heros.
